findings.title: Verification and negative-walk close failures can remain authoritative
findings.detail: verifyMembership opens temporary child directories, but its finally catches closeOwned failure and ignores it. closeOwned marks released then invokes close, without latching uncertainty itself. With valid membership and a failed temporary close, walk can return true and verify can remain true, losing cleanup evidence and leaking an uncertain allocation. retainAbsent likewise suppresses intermediate-parent close failures; those temporary descriptors are not registered for later closeAll, contrary to its comment. Existing injected-close cases arm at final release or open enumeration, not verification or the intermediate negative walk. This is a static control-flow finding; no fault injection was executed by reviewer.
findings.proposed: Within existing private resources, preserve every close failure, latch uncertainty before a later proof can verify, and cover verify/negative temporary allocations without retrying numeric FDs.

findings.title: Proved absences are checked as positive files; dependency closure is incomplete
findings.detail: Reader concatenates consumed_paths and negative_lookups then requires workspaceRetained.has for every entry. An actually absent .film/subtitles.json or a heard-media transcript is intentionally null and entered in the closure negative ledger, never the positive file map: a legitimate default/untranscribed case is refused with DEPENDENCY_UNPROVEN. Consumer directory_lookups/media_lookups are not cross-checked at this point. There is one precomputed supply pass rather than required bounded missing-dependency discovery. Existing tests assert new markers/unknown/removal refusals, not valid absent style/transcript or full dependency ledger correctness.
findings.proposed: Check positive, negative, directory and media dependencies against their appropriate existing private ledgers; supply missing safe dependencies within original bounds and assert legitimate absence as well as later birth rejection.

findings.title: Source identities are first retained after asynchronous digest and lineage reads
findings.detail: acquireNativeFacts computes digest and parses producer/film before opening retained source closure. An equal-byte source leaf/parent replacement after those asynchronous reads but before closure.open becomes the accepted initial identity; byte equality at retainFile cannot establish it is the identity at read admission. This is an in-progress round swap, not the independently new stable round permitted by MAIN clarification. The pending-round test changes workspace film only after a media child starts, long after source closure exists, and cannot expose this earlier source window.
findings.proposed: Retain and fence original source identity across the whole authority acquisition and add the originally required source/parent equal-byte replacement barrier case; retain separate fresh-round success semantics.

findings.title: Physical alias rejection and directory classification are unproved and incomplete
findings.detail: Regular-file checks contain no hardlink/nlink or cross-tree dev/ino alias check. Replacing a workspace leaf with a hardlink to committed source before a fresh read satisfies same bytes and regular-file checks, defeating physical independence even with two descriptor objects. Derived classification sees fileMembership only, so a preexisting unknown empty workspace directory (e.g. .film/history) has no classification branch. Pure empty-directory test proves a later file invalidates one closure, not physical independence or permitted directory set. These are static scenarios, not executed mutations.
findings.proposed: Establish existing safe-root/physical-tree invariants and explicit permitted directory membership, with same-path independent resources and hardlink/unknown-empty-directory vectors; no DTO change required.

findings.title: Page cache pairing accepts arbitrary key/dependencies and orphan film poster
findings.detail: Any 24hex pageframe triple passes if JSON files is an array of existing paths and stamp matches those paths, including an empty array with SHA256(empty) stamp; no binding of key to black/page/ms/width/overrides or required originating page is established. film-poster.jpg unconditionally returns. This is weaker than original approved producer/key/pairing requirement; these bytes are not expected media authority, so this finding is about cache admissibility, not a fabricated probe duration exploit. Tests cover probe cache only and never reach these page cache branches.
findings.proposed: Use exact existing pinned producer/key/pairing evidence for accepted page derivatives, or honestly reject unprovable pairing; add targeted original R04 cases rather than broaden whitelist or alter artifacts.

findings.title: Authority preflight bypasses retained text and descriptor budgets
findings.detail: streamDigest calls handle.readFile on nonmedia before testing 8MiB; retained closure and total/path/depth limits are acquired only after this graph walk. Thus a huge referenced text allocates before limit rejection; many sublimit texts can accumulate in cache without 64MiB guard. nativeLineage separately permits up to64MiB JSON. No FD estimate/instance budget exists before per-leaf parent chains:4096 paths can allocate many more than4096 descriptors, reaching EMFILE rather than controlled admission. Pure closure text tests cannot detect authority preflight allocations because they never invoke acquireNativeFacts.
findings.proposed: Apply approved limits before and during the actual authority reads and estimate descriptor allocations within existing instance policy; verify original growth/path/depth/resource error cases under a future exact grant.

findings.title: Cleanup reporting differs before and after transfer
findings.detail: Authority catch invokes closure.close before rethrow: if close throws it replaces primary instead of retaining primary plus causes. Reader delivered-handle and ordinary failed-read cleanup paths latch cleanupUncertain and throw causes locally, but do not append to cleanupFailures; reader.close reports only cleanupFailures (populated for late adopt cleanup). Therefore reader.close can resolve after a delivered release failed, despite its comment promising real cleanup reporting. Current delivered failure test checks only later read rejection, never reader.close failure/cause preservation. Existing Expected primary+cleanup tests use faultyReader, not these implementations.
findings.proposed: Preserve original primary plus all cleanup causes and keep uncertainty observable across new-reader close without reattempting any allocation; extend the original before/after transfer cases.

findings.title: Facts guard does not revisit producer/consumer DB lineage
findings.detail: Initial nativeLineage checks adopted-source/adoption/impact plan and consumer graph. assertCurrent later checks closure.verify and canonicalDigest(#bind), whose fields come from owner, committed transaction, snapshot row and creation.sourceFact. Changes/corruption to created_impact_fact.plan_sha256/plan_json or adopted lineage facts after issue are outside that digest, so a held lease can remain current after its original producer authority is no longer provable. The source-lease test only checks instance brand/clone rejection, not post-issue DB lineage corruption. Current workspace guard checks active commit/owner but not control; binding.isCurrent supplies session/control fence via Expected, not independent new-reader DB evidence.
findings.proposed: Retain a synchronous authority fence over original relevant producer bindings using existing private stores, and assert the original post-issue DB/owner/commit/generation fault vectors; leave selection-ledger and HTTP/Ack integration for later tickets.

findings.title: Probe success and one cancel case leave original media/failure semantics unproved
findings.detail: Actual held-FD ffprobe and close-child evidence are meaningful. But R05 compares only video duration/audio/fps against locally reimplemented normalization and merely checks digest hex shape; 3s color fixture has no rotated/multi-video-stream vector. No timeout/output overrun/spawn/nonzero/malformed tool, hanging child, duration-vs-trim/subtitle mismatch or probe-time source/parent replacement case exists in the26 tests. A normalization/provenance or output-limit defect can leave all those current assertions green.
findings.proposed: Cover those explicit original N1N2 semantics with real diagnostic tools/media and narrow branch assertions under MAIN-approved future commands; do not call diagnostics Chinese films or require V1 integration for component acceptance.

findings.title: Ordering oracle and environment evidence do not establish consumer parity
findings.detail: Component fixture reuses a single video asset for its shots; its self-sorted listing is insensitive to numeric-order defects. Multi-path pure test exercises reader helper and a second handwritten locale sort, not actual pinned listFiles, and has no real caption translation-directory order comparator. ICU/locale existence assertions do not record their values. Source static comparison supports numeric rule, but real filesystem consumer parity required by R06 remains unproved.
findings.proposed: Use the original multi-video/nonASCII real FS listing comparison against pinned consumer plus separate caption order and actual environment fingerprint; no new ordering contract.
